component.name: Kori
component.summary: Cooling, lighting and LCD control for supported hardware

description.p: Kori drives an NZXT Kraken cooler from Linux without a vendor agent: pump and fan curves, the RGB controller, and the picture on the LCD panel. It is unofficial, and is neither affiliated with nor endorsed by NZXT.

Nothing is written to hardware that the device has not first proven it can do. A capability the machine did not confirm is reported as unknown and the matching control stays disabled with the reason, rather than being offered on a guess.

ul.li: Pump and fan duty curves, revalidated against safety floors before every write
Liquid, CPU, memory and GPU telemetry sampled by independent collectors
Lighting control gated on a firmware revision validated on real hardware
LCD panel presets, previewed with the same renderer that feeds the glass
A background daemon that owns the devices, serializes writes and detects a competing writer
Neither binary runs as root, and normal operation opens no network socket

screenshot.caption: System and cooling state at a glance
Pump, fan and the onboard liquid-temperature curve
The controller's channels, and the panel on the Kraken

ul.li: The installed icon is now a file an icon theme can decode, so the window carries the application artwork instead of a placeholder
Pump and fan curves, telemetry, lighting and LCD panel presets over a local daemon
Lighting and panel writes gated on firmware revisions validated on owned hardware
Wayland and X11, with no elevated privileges and no network access
